decisive_items: bilateral facial nerve enhancement compatible with bilateral facial neuritis
bilateral facial drooping, inability to close her eyelids, and difficulty raising her eyebrows
bilateral lower motor neuron facial muscle weakness
response.rationale: MRI directly confirms bilateral facial neuritis, matching the focal cranial nerve findings; R1 is the same but less specific. Other candidates lack imaging support or are excluded by normal labs.

rejected.why: Sjögren antibody normal excludes Sjögren's syndrome
Peripheral neuropathy is grade 1 and stable, not the acute facial presentation
Chemotherapy neuropathy typically distal sensory, not bilateral facial nerve enhancement
No supportive evidence for GBS; MRI shows facial neuritis not polyradiculopathy
Underlying cancer is background, not the acute neurological diagnosis
Capillary leak caused edema but not facial nerve palsy
Less specific than R1C; bilateral facial neuritis is the precise finding
Peripheral neuropathy is too general and not the cause of facial palsy
Nab-paclitaxel neuropathy does not explain facial nerve enhancement
Paraneoplastic syndrome lacks supporting antibodies or typical pattern
Lyme titers normal excludes Lyme disease
